description: Behavioral routing eval fixture. Each case is a task description as a user would phrase it, paired with the agent the routing table should select. Consumed by test/validate-routing.test.js (static, CI, free) and scripts/eval-routing.mjs (model-in-the-loop, opt-in). Each case declares a basis: canonical cases are forced by a verbatim anchor in the routing context the model sees (a miss means fix the routing table or the model); judgment cases encode the fixture author's reading and name the contested alternative (a miss means review the fixture first).

cases.task: Users report the export button does nothing on Safari. No error in the server logs. Find out why.
cases.why: Broken behavior, root cause unknown — investigation, not implementation.

cases.task: Add a POST /api/invoices endpoint. Request schema is {customerId: string, lineItems: LineItem[]}, response is {id: string, total: number}. Acceptance: returns 422 on empty lineItems. Target files: src/routes/invoices.ts, src/services/invoice.ts. Architecture is settled.
cases.why: Schemas, acceptance criteria, target files, architecture settled — the full readiness gate is met.

cases.task: Where is the rate limiting implemented and what calls into it?
cases.why: Codebase lookup with cross-file tracing, no change requested.

cases.task: Does this repo have any retry logic for outbound webhooks? Find any reference to it.
cases.why: "does X exist" / "find any reference" is an explicit Scout signal in the routing table.

cases.task: Review the changes on this branch before I open the PR.
cases.why: Quality assessment of changed code.

cases.task: The settings page feels cluttered and the visual hierarchy is unclear. What should change?
cases.why: Visual hierarchy judgment, no spec — a design decision, not an implementation.

cases.task: Our services all import from a shared kernel package that imports back from two of them. Is this structure defensible?

cases.task: Should we migrate from REST to GraphQL for the internal admin API?

cases.task: 500 error on the login endpoint with a NullPointerException stack trace.

cases.anchor: Stack trace / exception / failing test / "debug" language

cases.task: The report job got slow last week and now it's failing with OOMKilled in the pod logs.
cases.why: Judgment — OOMKilled is a crash signal but not literal stack-trace/exception language, so Rule 1 is inferred, not matched; Rule 3's "slow" matches literally.

cases.task: The checkout integration test started failing on CI after yesterday's merge.
cases.why: Rule 1 — failing test is a debugging signal, not a request for more tests.

cases.why: Judgment — no explicit vulnerability language, so Rule 3's literal "slow" match competes with Rule 2; the injection surface is the dominant concern.

cases.task: Review this PR specifically for exploitable input handling in the file upload path.

cases.task: The orders page runs one SQL query per order row and takes 4 seconds to render with 500 orders.

cases.task: Run npm run lint and paste me the raw output. No analysis needed.
cases.why: Command execution with no judgment requested — the routing table's command execution signal, with no failing-test language to trigger Rule 1.

cases.why: Judgment — explicit request for a direct answer, but a datastore choice is arguably system design.

cases.task: What do you think of this codebase overall?
cases.why: Judgment — unscoped opinion with no bounded artifact, but "this codebase" invites a quality review.
